rationale:
Positives: The agent verified the user correctly using full name and zip, found the correct account, and identified the order containing the water bottle and desk lamp. They also looked up product variants before proposing options. 

Failures against policy: 
- The agent executed an order-changing write (exchange_delivered_order_items) without first explicitly stating the exact changes and obtaining explicit confirmation to proceed. Asking the user to pick variants is not the same as confirming the order-changing action; the policy requires a clear confirmation step before committing changes. 
- When the user asked to proceed with only the desk lamp exchange, the agent stated that the exchange could not be changed or canceled without any tool-based verification. This is an unsupported claim and contradicts the requirement to avoid fabricating information and to inspect order status/eligibility before asserting limits. It also fails to complete the user’s final request. 
- The agent did not verify order status/eligibility before performing the exchange (the tool call name suggests a delivered order, but no status check was shown). 

Given these issues—especially performing the exchange without explicit confirmation and providing an unsupported refusal to adjust—the interaction does not meet the pass bar.
